title: Simple positive divided powers generate the positive integral Kostant form
statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with splitting Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, reduced crystallographic root system $R$, positive roots $R^+$ and simple roots $\Delta$. Fix a Chevalley basis $h_i,e_\alpha$ in the conventions of [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw]: the $h_i$ are the simple coroots, $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$, $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$, and $[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=\pm(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)e_{\alpha+\beta}$ when $\alpha+\beta\in R$, with zero bracket if the sum is neither a root nor zero; $p_{\alpha,\beta}=\max\{q\geq0:\beta-q\alpha\in R\}$. Write $U_{\mathbf Q}=T_{\mathbf Q}(\mathfrak g)/(xy-yx-[x,y])$ and $e_\alpha^{(m)}=e_\alpha^m/m!$ for $m\geq0$. Let $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$ be the unital $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra of $U_{\mathbf Q}$ generated by $e_\beta^{(m)}$ for all $\beta\in R^+$ and $m\geq0$. Then
$$K_{\mathbf Z}^+=\mathbf Z\langle e_\alpha^{(m)}:\alpha\in\Delta,\ m\geq0\rangle.$$
Equivalently, every positive-root divided power is an integer linear combination of finite words in simple-positive-root divided powers. The assertion is over $\mathbf Z$, before any reduction of scalars, and includes $R=\varnothing$, when both algebras are $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Section 1, printed pp.150--151: integral form generated by simple divided powers and its hyperalgebra realization. Read online at https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf; the local PDF is WANTED. proof.text: Let $S$ be the unital $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by all simple-positive divided powers. Prove $e_\gamma^{(n)}\in S$ for every positive root by strong induction on $n$, with an inner strong induction on the positive integer height $h(\gamma)$ (sum of simple coordinates). At $n=0$ the element is $1$. For every $n$, a simple $\gamma$ is a generator of $S$. Fix $n\geq1$ and a nonsimple $\gamma$, assuming the assertions for all exponents below $n$ at all positive roots, and for exponent $n$ at all smaller positive heights.

source.place: Agent proof of positive integral generation using root chains (Appendix C.21--C.22, p.612), the bottom-of-string divided-adjoint identity, and the assumed Chevalley normalization (Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509). Mathieu Section 1, pp.150--151, read online, gives the simple-divided-power convention but omits this comparison proof.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition], the roots $\alpha$ and coroots $h_\alpha$ form a finite reduced crystallographic root pairing for the evaluation pairing $\mathfrak h^\vee\times\mathfrak h\to\mathbf Q$. By [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans], applied with $J=\Delta$, every coroot or its negative is a nonnegative integral sum of the simple coroots, which are linearly independent; with the sign-coherent root coordinates of $\Delta$ this makes $\Delta$ a base of this root pairing in the sense of [lem-sfb-positive-root-simple-chain], and positivity there is positivity of the height. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-root-simple-chain] to this root pairing and base. The chain has length $h(\gamma)\geq2$. Its last simple root $a$ and its penultimate sum $c$ satisfy $\gamma=c+a$, with $c\in R^+$. Some simple coordinate of $c$ outside $a$ is positive: otherwise reducedness would give $c=a$, and $\gamma=2a$ would not be a root. Thus $a,c$ are linearly independent. Let $p$ be the largest nonnegative integer with $c-pa\in R$ and put $b=c-pa$. The root-string interval [lem-sfb-root-string-integer-interval] gives $b-a\notin R$: otherwise $p+1$ would be in the same string. Coordinates outside $a$ are unchanged and include a positive one, so the same-sign property of root coordinates makes $b$ positive. Put $k=p+1\geq1$. Then $\gamma=b+ka$ and $h(b)=h(\gamma)-k<h(\gamma)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-string-divided-adjoint-triangular] to these positive independent roots $a,b$, integer $k$ and exponent $n$. Every term $e_a^{(kn-j)}e_b^{(n)}e_a^{(j)}$ lies in $S$: $a$ is simple and the inner induction gives $e_b^{(n)}\in S$. Every correction monomial lies in $S$ by the outer induction, since each of its factors has exponent strictly below $n$. Subtract the integral correction from the displayed sum to obtain $\varepsilon^n e_\gamma^{(n)}\in S$. Multiplication by $\varepsilon^n\in\{1,-1\}$ gives $e_\gamma^{(n)}\in S$. This closes both strong inductions; it never divides by a root-string constant or reduces scalars.

proof.text: Every generator of $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$ now belongs to $S$, giving $K_{\mathbf Z}^+\subseteq S$. Conversely each simple root is positive, so each generator of $S$ belongs to $K_{\mathbf Z}^+$; hence equality. The integer span of finite words in the simple divided powers contains $1$ (empty word) and the generators and is closed under sums, negatives and products by distributivity, so it is exactly $S$, proving the equivalent formulation. When $R=\varnothing$, both generating sets are empty and both unital integer subalgebras are $\mathbf Z$.
